title: 10 Best Eats in Kobe Chinatown (Nankinmachi)
description: The best food in Kobe Chinatown (Nankinmachi) — curated from Reddit reviews. Pork buns, xiaolongbao, gyoza, Kobe beef & more. Interactive map included.

places.name: Roushouki (老祥記)

redditQuotes.text: Nankin-machi (Chinatown) is really lively and bustling — the pork buns there are incredible. Roushouki always has a line but it's worth the wait.

places.verdict: The undisputed icon of Nankinmachi, operating since the Taisho era.

comparison.best for: Pork Buns in 1-3-7 Motomachi-dori, Chuo-ku with a ¥500–¥1,000 (5-pack) spend range
comparison.strengths: 4.1★ from 2,529 Google reviews · Pork Buns · 1-3-7 Motomachi-dori, Chuo-ku
comparison.why it made the list: The undisputed icon of Nankinmachi, operating since the Taisho era. Expect a 20-30 minute wait at peak times — they sometimes sell out by evening. Go early. The five-pack minimum sounds like a lot until you start eating them.
comparison.what to order: Roushouki (老祥記), located at 1-3-7 Motomachi-dori, Chuo-ku, is famous for its butaman (pork buns), sold in packs of five. These tiny buns are packed with a rich, juicy pork filling, and the dough has a subtle sweetness that perfectly complements the savory meat.

places.name: YUNYUN

redditQuotes.text: YUNYUN's xiaolongbao are the thing I dream about after visiting Kobe. Crispy bottom, soup inside — totally different from Shanghai-style ones.

places.verdict: Started as a rice noodle maker, now famous for these pan-fried beauties.

comparison.best for: Xiaolongbao in 1-3-17 Motomachi-dori, Chuo-ku with a ¥450–¥900 spend range
comparison.strengths: 4.1★ from 921 Google reviews · Xiaolongbao · 1-3-17 Motomachi-dori, Chuo-ku
comparison.limitations: moves fast — you can watch them fold dumplings through the glass while you wait
comparison.why it made the list: Started as a rice noodle maker, now famous for these pan-fried beauties. The line looks intimidating but moves fast — you can watch them fold dumplings through the glass while you wait. Eat-in space on the second floor.
comparison.what to order: YUNYUN, located at 1-3-17 Motomachi-dori, Chuo-ku, serves pan-fried xiaolongbao at ¥450 for 3 or ¥900 for 6. These xiaolongbao are crispy on the bottom and juicy inside, so poke a hole first and sip the hot soup before biting in to avoid burning yourself.

places.name: Gyoza Daigaku (餃子大学)

redditQuotes.text: Gyoza Daigaku literally means 'Gyoza University' — they're that confident. The crispy-on-one-side, juicy-on-the-other gyoza are an institution in Kobe Chinatown.

comparison.best for: Gyoza in Nankinmachi, Chuo-ku with a ¥600–¥1,000 spend range
comparison.strengths: 4★ from 795 Google reviews · Gyoza · Nankinmachi, Chuo-ku
comparison.why it made the list: Tiny shop, big reputation. Arrive before the 5pm opening to beat the line. The minimum 14-piece order is generous — the gyoza are perfectly balanced between crispy and juicy. Counter seats let you watch the kitchen action.
comparison.what to order: Gyoza Daigaku (餃子大学), located in Nankinmachi, Chuo-ku, specializes in fried gyoza, with a minimum order of 14 pieces (a 2-person serving). You can choose with or without garlic (ninniku) and pair it with a tall draft beer, as that's the entire menu and all you need.

places.name: Shikohroh (四興樓)

redditQuotes.text: Pro tip — Shikohroh has just as good nikuman without the crazy wait time. Plus they're a full Chinese restaurant so you can sit down and eat properly.

comparison.best for: Chinese in Near Motomachi Station with a ¥400–¥1,200 spend range
comparison.strengths: 4★ from 618 Google reviews · Chinese · Near Motomachi Station
comparison.why it made the list: The insider's alternative to Roushouki. Slightly tucked away but right across from Motomachi Station. The nikuman are plump and generous with filling. If you want a sit-down meal beyond street snacks, this is your spot.
comparison.what to order: Shikohroh (四興樓), located near Motomachi Station, is a Chinese restaurant where you should order the nikuman (steamed pork buns), which are just as good as Roushouki's but without the long line. Also try their old-school Chinese ramen and chukadon (stir-fried rice bowl).

places.name: Kissho-ki (吉祥吉)

redditQuotes.text: If you want proper Kobe beef, go to an actual restaurant and pay ¥8,000-¥15,000. The street stalls claiming A5 for $10 are not the real deal.

places.verdict: Facing the central plaza, Kissho-ki is one of the more reputable Kobe beef stalls in Nankinmachi.

comparison.best for: Kobe Beef in 2-1-14 Motomachi-dori, Chuo-ku with a ¥300–¥1,000 spend range
comparison.strengths: 3.8★ from 235 Google reviews · Kobe Beef · 2-1-14 Motomachi-dori, Chuo-ku
comparison.limitations: the sushi at ¥300 per piece is a fun, affordable taste
comparison.why it made the list: Facing the central plaza, Kissho-ki is one of the more reputable Kobe beef stalls in Nankinmachi. Keep expectations realistic — street-stall Kobe beef won't rival a proper teppanyaki restaurant, but the sushi at ¥300 per piece is a fun, affordable taste. Don't expect a melt-in-your-mouth A5 experience here.
comparison.what to order: Kissho-ki (吉祥吉), located at 2-1-14 Motomachi-dori, Chuo-ku, offers Kobe beef lean skewers for ¥1,000 each and Kobe beef sushi for ¥300 a piece. The skewers let you choose your preferred cut, while the sushi offers the best value for a quick taste.

places.name: Tenshido & Character Bun Stalls (天仁堂)

redditQuotes.text: The cute panda buns are everywhere in Nankinmachi — they're filled with black sesame paste and make for great photos.

places.verdict: Multiple shops sell these adorable buns, so walk the full street and compare before buying.

comparison.best for: Character Buns in Along Nankinmachi main street with a ¥200–¥500 spend range
comparison.strengths: 4.4★ from 62 Google reviews · Character Buns · Along Nankinmachi main street
comparison.why it made the list: Multiple shops sell these adorable buns, so walk the full street and compare before buying. They're Instagrammable, genuinely tasty, and cheap. The Piyo-man with custard cream is our favorite. Perfect palate-cleanser between savory snacks.
comparison.what to order: Tenshido & Character Bun Stalls (天仁堂), located along Nankinmachi main street, offers character buns like the Piyo-man (chick bun, custard cream filling), Panda-man (black sesame paste filling), and Buta-man (savory pork). Also look for the Shishi-man (lion dance, purple sweet potato) and Tora-man (tiger, cream filling).

Also look for the Shishi-man (lion dance, purple sweet potato) and Tora-man (tiger, cream filling).

places.name: Mikiya (三木屋)
places.verdict: Founded in 1947 as a fruit store, Mikiya directly sources their own produce — so the quality is a cut above the other candied fruit stalls.

comparison.best for: Candied Fruits in 1-3-16 Sakaemachi-dori, Chuo-ku with a ¥400–¥600 spend range
comparison.strengths: 3.5★ from 60 Google reviews · Candied Fruits · 1-3-16 Sakaemachi-dori, Chuo-ku
comparison.why it made the list: Founded in 1947 as a fruit store, Mikiya directly sources their own produce — so the quality is a cut above the other candied fruit stalls. The contrast between the crispy sugar shell and the fresh strawberry inside is addictive.
comparison.what to order: Mikiya (三木屋), located at 1-3-16 Sakaemachi-dori, Chuo-ku, is known for its strawberry candy, priced at ¥500 per bottle. This crispy candy coating over juicy, sweet-tart strawberries is the perfect palate cleanser after all the savory, oily street food.

places.verdict: The perfect ending to a Nankinmachi food crawl.

places.name: Yuen Kee (元記)

redditQuotes.text: Yuen Kee if you like dim sum.

places.verdict: When you're tired of standing and eating, Yuen Kee offers a proper sit-down dim sum experience.

comparison.best for: Dim Sum in Nankinmachi, Chuo-ku with a ¥800–¥2,000 spend range
comparison.strengths: 4★ from 509 Google reviews · Dim Sum · Nankinmachi, Chuo-ku
comparison.why it made the list: When you're tired of standing and eating, Yuen Kee offers a proper sit-down dim sum experience. It's not Hong Kong-level dim sum, but it's solid and reasonably priced. A good option if you want a full meal rather than snack-hopping.
comparison.what to order: Yuen Kee (元記), located in Nankinmachi, Chuo-ku, is a dim sum restaurant where you should order the dim sum selection, including har gow, siu mai, and char siu bao. This is a great place for a proper sit-down dim sum meal if you want to escape the street-food scrum.
